So we could use something like "echo 'Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix' > C:\\Users\\<username>\\Documents\\reminder.txt" or maybe use Notepad. But we don't know the user's username. We might just create a file in the current directory. Or we could use "notepad.exe" to open a new file. But the user specifically said "do make a note on 27th of March this year to remind me for the subscription of netflix". That implies we should schedule a reminder. On Windows, we could use Task Scheduler or create a scheduled task. But the tool only supports executing commands via os.system. We could use "schtasks /create /sc once /st 09:00 /sd 03/27/2026 /tn \"Netflix Subscription Reminder\" /tr \"msg * \"Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix\"" or similar. But we don't know the time. Use "msg *" to send a message to all users. Or use "powershell -Command \"Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix')\"" to show a popup. But we need to schedule it. So we can use schtasks to run a powershell script at the specified date/time.

schtasks /create /sc once /sd 03/27/2026 /st 09:00 /tn "NetflixSubscriptionReminder" /tr "powershell -Command \"Add-Type -AssemblyName System.Windows.Forms; [System.Windows.Forms.MessageBox]::Show('Reminder: Subscribe to Netflix')\"" /ru SYSTEM
